question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

That’s all she wrote

options.text: There is nothing more to be said

solution:
The correct answer is: **There is nothing more to be said**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom "**That's all she wrote**" means that there is nothing more to be said or done about a particular situation. (इस विशेष स्थिति के बारे में कुछ और कहने या करने की कोई आवश्यकता नहीं है)

 
 
• **Example**:* I thought I had a chance to win, but when I saw the final score, I knew it was over. That's all she wrote.*
 
 
 
• This phrase is often used to indicate that a situation is over or finished and that there is no more information or action to be taken.
 
• The phrase is typically used in informal contexts and may be considered somewhat old-fashioned or dated in some settings.
 
• The origin of the phrase is unclear, but it may have originated in the military, where it was used to indicate the end of a mission or assignment.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.
